newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-DAVENPORT OVERPOWERS FERNANDEZ AT EVERT CUP.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-DAVENPORT OVERPOWERS FERNANDEZ AT EVERT CUP.

text.p: In a match between two former friends, fourth seed Lindsay Davenport overpowered ninth seed Mary Joe Fernandez 6-1 6-1 Friday in the semifinals of the Evert Cup.
The eighth-ranked Davenport plays sixth seed Irina Spirlea of Romania for the Evert Cup title Saturday. It will be their first oncourt meeting.

Davenport, who won her eighth career title at Oklahoma City a few weeks ago, pressured Fernandez with her big serve and brawny style of play. While Davenport scored 25 outright winners and only eight unforced errors, Fernandez had 23 unforced errors and only 13 clearcut winners.

"She just played too well," said Fernandez, a former two-time Evert Cup champion. "She came out firing. She's such a big girl and hits the ball so hard that unless I can somehow dictate the rally, I'm in big trouble."
In the first set of a match that lasted a scant 52 minutes, Fernandez held her serve only once, at love in the fifth game. In her other three service games in the set, she won a total of four points.
Fernandez won the fifth game in the second set by breaking Davenport's serve. She won only six points in her own three service games in the last set.

At one time, Davenport and the 14th-ranked Fernandez were the best of friends and the best of doubles partners. In 1996, the tandem won four titles, including the French Open and the year-end championships.
But a misunderstanding at the end of last year caused a rift between the two.

Davenport apparently heard rumours that Fernandez wasn't planning to play a full schedule this year. Instead of checking with Fernandez, who says she always intended to play the entire year, Davenport went out and found a new doubles partner.
"I read about it in the paper the next day," said Fernandez. "She still hadn't told me. It puts a little damper on things."
Fernandez indicated that it is unlikely the two will ever be pals again.

"We were good friends and we're not any more. It's a competitive world, the tennis world. People look after themselves. We've always said it's hard to have friendships in tennis because you're always competing against one another. It's been proven that's the case."
Davenport seemed to have a different version of the spat and would not elaborate on the particulars.

"We're not as close as we used to be. We're talking and working on everything. It's really between us. The good thing is, hopefully, we're working on it. She's always been my best friend. I think she always will be."
